agent.protocol:
# Response protocol
- When you make a significant decision (what to read, what to change, how to verify), write a line that starts with "DECISION:" followed by a short explanation in a single sentence.
- Work only inside the project folder (and the additional folders, if listed) and only with the tools available to you.
- ALWAYS end your response with this block, as valid JSON (keep the keys and the outcome values exactly as shown):
```regia
{"esito": "ok" | "ko" | "bloccato", "sintesi": "result in 1-3 sentences, useful to the next phase", "decisioni": ["main decision and reason", "..."]}
```
"esito" is the outcome, "sintesi" the summary, "decisioni" the list of decisions. Use "ko" if the task did not succeed (e.g. failing tests), "bloccato" if you cannot proceed without human intervention (explain what is needed in "sintesi").
If you stop because you lack the tools to do it, add "permesso" (permission) to the block: "modifica" if you need to edit files or run commands, "internet" if you need to use the web: the person supervising can grant it with one click.
If you stop because you need to read or write in a folder outside the allowed ones, add "cartella" (folder) to the block with the absolute path of the folder: this too can be granted with one click.
agent.protocolPoints: - You are in a review phase: if you find concrete changes to make, add the "punti" key (the list of points) to the block, with the proposed corrections, one per item, each as an object {"testo": "file or function, problem and fix", "priorita": "alta" | "bassa"} ("testo" is the text, "priorita" the priority): "alta" (high) for bugs and important changes, "bassa" (low) for minor or unimportant suggestions (style, naming, small simplifications). Order them by priority, most important first, at most {max}: if you find more, merge similar ones. The person approving will choose which ones to apply. Finding points does not make the task unsuccessful: still use "ok". With nothing to report, leave the key out.
agent.continue: Continue from where you left off.
agent.continueTurns:
You ran out of turns before finishing. Continue from where you left off without redoing work already done: check the state of the files you were changing, complete the task going straight to the goal (avoid unnecessary exploration) and end with the outcome block. If you cannot finish, end with outcome "bloccato" explaining what is missing.

{protocol}

uat.context:
# Acceptance test on the device
Regia has already built, installed and opened the app.
- Device: {device}
- App (applicationId): {app}
- adb: "{adb}" (always use -s {serial})
- Folder for screenshots: {dir}
- App log, recorded by Regia (the app's warnings, errors, crashes and ANRs): {log}

## How to proceed
1. Understand what changed: goal, previous phases and `git diff` (if the changes are already committed, `git show --stat HEAD`). Pick 3 to 8 scenarios focused on the change, plus a quick check that the app starts and its main screen works.
2. For each scenario: read the screen, act, check the expected result. Save a screenshot at the key moment and look at it with Read when a visual check is needed. After each scenario reread the last lines of the app log (tail) and link errors to the actions just performed.
3. Report anomalies and the scenarios to try by hand in the final block.

## Useful commands
- Screen as text: `"{adb}" -s {serial} shell uiautomator dump /sdcard/regia-ui.xml` then `"{adb}" -s {serial} exec-out cat /sdcard/regia-ui.xml` (texts, resource-id and bounds [x1,y1][x2,y2]: tap the center).
- Tap, text, swipe, keys: `shell input tap X Y`, `shell input text "word%sword"` (%s is a space), `shell input swipe X1 Y1 X2 Y2 300`, `shell input keyevent 4` (back) or `66` (enter).
- Screenshot: `"{adb}" -s {serial} exec-out screencap -p > "{dir}/01-name.png"` (progressive number and short scenario name).
- Clean app restart: `shell am force-stop {app}` then `shell monkey -p {app} -c android.intent.category.LAUNCHER 1`.
{windows}
## Rules
- Do not modify the project code and do not commit.
- No irreversible actions or actions with real effects: purchases, payments, sending real messages or emails, deleting data or accounts, changing device settings.
- Do not clear the logcat buffer: Regia is following it.
- If credentials are needed use only those given in the phase instructions; otherwise stop with outcome "bloccato" explaining what is needed.
- Be efficient: read the screen as text and use screenshots only where needed, they cost more.
uat.windows: - On Windows prefix adb commands that contain device paths (e.g. /sdcard/...) with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 `, otherwise the shell turns them into Windows paths.
uat.unknownApp: not detected: find it with `shell dumpsys window | grep mCurrentFocus`

agent.pr:
# Pull request to read
{url}

Read the pull request and all its comments, without changing files and without replying on the PR.
- GitHub: details and general comments with `gh pr view <url> --comments`; the discussions on code lines, with their state, with GraphQL (the REST API does not tell whether a discussion is resolved):
  `gh api graphql -F owner=<owner> -F name=<repo> -F number=<number> -f query='query($owner:String!,$name:String!,$number:Int!){repository(owner:$owner,name:$name){pullRequest(number:$number){reviewThreads(first:100){nodes{id isResolved isOutdated path line comments(first:20){nodes{author{login} body}}}}}}}'`
- Azure DevOps: `az repos pr show --id <number>` and the threads with `az devops invoke --area git --resource pullRequestThreads --route-parameters project=<project> repositoryId=<repo> pullRequestId=<number>`; consider only threads with status active or pending.
- Otherwise open the address with WebFetch.
If the required tool is not installed or you are not authenticated, stop with outcome "bloccato" and explain what is needed.

How to choose the points:
1. Leave out resolved discussions (isResolved), those outdated by later commits (isOutdated) and messages without a change request.
2. A comment listing several findings (for example the summary of a review bot) becomes one point per finding.
3. For each remaining finding verify on the project's current code (current branch, including uncommitted changes) that the problem is still there: do not trust the comment's description or the replies, open the cited files and search with Grep for the names involved (keys, functions, resource files) across the whole project. If it is already fixed, do not put it in the points: add it to the "sistemati" (already fixed) key of the outcome block, one item per finding (severity, file, problem and why it is fixed).
4. Do not drop open findings based on your own judgement (for example WARNINGs not introduced by the PR): the approver decides.

Each point is an object {"testo": "file and line, problem, fix to make, comment author, and at the end Verified: what you checked in the code to confirm the problem is still there", "gravita": "BLOCKER" | "CRITICAL" | "MAJOR" | "MINOR" | "WARNING" | "INFO" | "NIT", "priorita": "alta" | "bassa"} ("testo" is the text, "gravita" the severity, "priorita" the priority). Use the severity stated in the comment; if missing, infer it (bugs and explicitly requested changes: MAJOR; optional suggestions: MINOR or NIT). Regia orders the points by severity, from BLOCKER down. Merge duplicate comments.
Check with git that the current branch is the PR branch: if it is not, say so in the summary, without switching branch. In the summary give the PR title, author and branch, how many open points you found per severity and how many are already fixed.

The linked user stories (above) are the reference: the fixes must respect their specification and acceptance criteria (all of them, if more than one). If the fix asked by a comment contradicts them, keep the point, start the text with "Conflicts with the US:", explain why and add "contrastoUs": true to the object, so the approver can decide.

Replies on the PR: for each finding already fixed and each point conflicting with the US prepare a reply to publish under the original comment, in the "risposte" (replies) key of the outcome block: [{"motivo": "sistemato" | "contrasto", "riferimento": "severity and file:line", "thread": "id of the discussion of the comment you reply to (id field of reviewThreads)", "testo": "the reply"}] ("motivo" is the reason: already fixed or conflicting; "riferimento" the reference). The text is short, polite and in the language of the comment you reply to: for "sistemato" say where and how it is fixed (file and, if you know it, the commit); for "contrasto" quote the user story acceptance criterion the change would contradict. The reply is published only under that comment: if the finding comes from a general comment (not in a code discussion), leave "thread" empty and Regia will not publish it. Do not publish anything yourself: Regia publishes a reply only if the approver confirms it.
